title: Affine etale diagonal complement lowers fibre degree
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T,T'$ be affine $S$-schemes, and let $a:T'\to T$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $n\geq1$ bound the degrees of the fibres of $a$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound], meaning that every residue-field fibre is finite of coordinate-algebra dimension at most $n$. Write $T''=T'\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $\pi_0,\pi_1$, and let $\delta:T'\to T''$ be the diagonal. Then $\delta$ identifies $T'$ with an open and closed subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], and its complementary open and closed subscheme $T^*$ is affine. The restriction $b=\pi_1|_{T^*}:T^*\to T'$ is etale and its fibre degrees are bounded by $n-1$. For every field $K$ and map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T'$, the fibre of $\pi_1$ is the disjoint union of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and the fibre of $b$; its coordinate $K$-algebra is $K\times C$, with $C$ the coordinate algebra of that complementary fibre and $\dim_K C\leq n-1$. If $n=1$, then $T^*$ is empty and $a$ is an open immersion.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $T'=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $T''=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R=B\otimes_A B$, and the projections are induced by the two factor maps. The morphism $a$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], so its diagonal is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It is also an open immersion: [def-weil-etale-morphism] makes $a$ unramified, and [def-weil-unramified-morphism] defines this using its open diagonal. Thus $\delta$ identifies $T'$ with an open subscheme $D\subseteq T''$ whose underlying subset is also closed. The defining identities of the diagonal give $\pi_1\delta=\mathrm{id}_{T'}$.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, proof, third paragraph; Schemes Tags 01JQ, 01KN; Morphisms Tag 02GE

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], choose the idempotent $e\in R$ with $D=D(e)$ and complement $D(1-e)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], this complement, with its open subscheme structure, is $T^*=\operatorname{Spec}R_{1-e}$, hence affine. It is a closed subscheme as well: the localization $R_{1-e}$ is $R/(e)$, since inverting $1-e$ forces $e=0$ by $e(1-e)=0$, and conversely $e=0$ makes $1-e=1$ invertible. Thus its inclusion is induced by the quotient $R\twoheadrightarrow R/(e)$ and is a closed immersion by the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This proves the asserted open and closed decomposition with the specified complementary open structure.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, proof, third paragraph; Algebra Tag 00EE, lemma-disjoint-decomposition; Schemes Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine

proof.text: The projection $\pi_1:T''\to T'$ is the base change of $a$ along $a$, hence etale by clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Applying [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction] with source open $T^*$ and target open all of $T'$ proves that $b$ is etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-base-change] the degrees of the fibres of $\pi_1$ are bounded by the same integer $n$.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, proof, third paragraph; Morphisms Tags 02GO, 02GJ, 03J7

proof.text: Put $C_0=\Gamma(T^*,\mathcal O_{T^*})$. Restriction to the disjoint open cover $T''=D\amalg T^*$ gives a ring isomorphism $R\cong B\times C_0$: its inverse glues the two sections, with no compatibility condition because the overlap is empty. Here $\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)=B$ through $\delta$. The structure map of $\pi_1$ is $b_0\mapsto(b_0,b^\sharp(b_0))$, because $\pi_1\delta=\mathrm{id}$, so this is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras. Fix a field-valued point $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the coordinate algebras of the fibres of $\pi_1$ and $b$ are respectively $R\otimes_B K$ and $C=C_0\otimes_B K$. The explicit $K$-algebra isomorphism $R\otimes_B K\cong K\times C$ sends $(b_0,c)\otimes k$ to $(u^\sharp(b_0)k,c\otimes k)$. Its inverse sends $(k,0)$ to $(1,0)\otimes k$ and $(0,c\otimes k)$ to $(0,c)\otimes k$; these balanced maps are inverse on pure tensors. The corresponding scheme decomposition is precisely the pullback of $D\amalg T^*$: a morphism into a disjoint open cover is uniquely its restrictions to the inverse images of the two opens. The first piece is $\operatorname{Spec}K$, since $\pi_1|_D$ is the inverse of $\delta$; the second is the fibre of $b$.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, proof, third paragraph, diagonal fibre is one point; elementary sheaf gluing and explicit tensor-product calculation, with Schemes Tag 01JQ

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound-field-points] to $\pi_1$ with its bound from step 3. Its fibre over every $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T'$ is finite over $K$, of coordinate dimension at most $n$. Step 4 identifies this coordinate algebra with $K\times C$. Projection onto $C$ shows that $C$ is finite-dimensional: the projections of any finite spanning set span it. If $c_1,\ldots,c_d$ is a basis of $C$, then $(1,0),(0,c_1),\ldots,(0,c_d)$ is a basis of $K\times C$, so $1+d\leq n$ and $d\leq n-1$. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite over $K$ by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Taking $K=\kappa(t')$ for each $t'\in T'$ proves that $n-1$ bounds the fibre degrees of $b$ by [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. This also gives every asserted clause for arbitrary field-valued points, without assuming that $a$ itself is finite.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, proof, third paragraph, degree subtraction; Morphisms Tag 03J5, lemma-characterize-universally-bounded

proof.text: If $n=1$, every residue-field fibre of $b$ has zero-dimensional coordinate algebra, hence is the empty affine scheme. If a point $x\in T^*$ existed, with $t'=b(x)$, the maps $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to T^*$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t')$ would give a point of the fibre at $t'$ by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], a contradiction. Thus $T^*$ is empty. The diagonal is therefore surjective. Equivalence (4) with (3) in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] says that $a$ is radicial, and [lem-weil-pbc-radicial-etale-open] now makes $a$ an open immersion, using its original etale hypothesis. This includes the case $T'$ is empty.
